questions.question: Day 8 Practice (Restaurant & Dining Out): When talking about booking an auto ride (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My sister'?

options.a: Drop me station gate. yesterday
options.b: Drop me station gate.
options.c: I am booking an auto ride right now.
options.d: Please drop me off near gate 2 of the metro station.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Please drop me off near gate 2 of the metro station.".

questions.question: Day 8 Vocabulary (Restaurant & Dining Out): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'circle back'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: Return to a topic later for follow-up.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'circle back' means: return to a topic later for follow-up. Example: "Let us circle back to the timeline discussion."

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 1 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "మీ ఆలోచన బాగుంది కానీ మన బడ్జెట్ దానికి అనుమతించదు."
(Literal attempt: "Your thought good but budget not allow.")

options.a: While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it.
options.b: I am needing to your thought good but budget not allow.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: Your thought good but budget not allow.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it."

Use diplomatic contrast 'While your proposal is insightful...'.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 2 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "రేపటి మీటింగ్ 3 గంటలకు రీషెడ్యూల్ చేయవచ్చా?"
(Literal attempt: "Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?")

options.a: Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.d: I am needing to tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?"

Use 'Could we reschedule...' for polite professional requests.

questions.question:
Day 8 Telugu Scenario 3 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Word-by-word: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.c: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
